raw_arguments.content:
# 01_cover

Welcome everyone. Today we're diving into the 2024 JavaScript Rising Stars — the 9th edition of this annual report that tracks which JavaScript projects gained the most GitHub stars over the past year. This is one of the clearest signals we have for where developer attention and ecosystem energy is actually flowing.

The methodology is straightforward: count the net new GitHub stars added between January and December 2024, across projects curated by Best of JS. Stars aren't perfect — they reflect developer interest and buzz, not necessarily production usage — but at scale, they're a reliable leading indicator.

Key points: (1) 9th edition, GitHub stars added Jan–Dec 2024 (2) Curated by Best of JS (3) Audience: frontend engineers and engineering managers tracking ecosystem trends
Duration: 1 minute

---

# 02_top10

[Transition] Let's start with the headline numbers — the overall top 10 projects by stars added in 2024.

shadcn/ui dominated for the second consecutive year with +38,000 stars — roughly eleven thousand more than second-place Excalidraw. [Pause] That gap is significant. It tells us this wasn't a close race; shadcn/ui has a category-defining lead.

The rest of the top 10 is a fascinating mix: Excalidraw and AFFiNE represent the collaborative tools category, Bruno challenges Postman in API testing, and n8n brings AI-native workflow automation into the list. [Data] Notably, four of these ten projects — n8n, Flowise, Supabase, and AFFiNE — all have significant AI capabilities. That's 40% of the top 10.

Key points: (1) shadcn/ui leads with +38k, a commanding gap over #2 (2) Top 10 spans UI libs, whiteboards, API tools, AI platforms, and desktop tech (3) AI-capable projects dominate
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 03_shadcn

[Transition] Let's go deeper on the #1 winner — shadcn/ui.

Created in January 2023, it hit 39,500 stars in its first year. In 2024, it added 38,000 more, reaching 77,500 total. That kind of sustained year-over-year momentum is extremely rare for a JavaScript project.

The core insight is simple but powerful: developers own the code. You copy components into your project — they become yours to modify, extend, and maintain. No abstraction layer, no library lock-in. [Pause]

But 2024 added serious platform depth: a new CLI supporting Next.js, Remix, Vite, Laravel, and monorepos. A registry model that spawned derivative ecosystems like Motion-Primitives and Magic UI. And Vercel's v0 AI service generating shadcn/ui components on demand. That flywheel just keeps accelerating.

Key points: (1) 77.5k total stars, back-to-back #1 (2) Copy-paste ownership model as key differentiator (3) CLI, registry, and AI integration created platform effects
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 04_frameworks

[Transition] Now let's look at the framework category, where the biggest surprise of 2024 happened.

htmx — a library that lets you add AJAX, WebSockets, and interactivity via simple HTML attributes — overtook React as the #1 front-end framework by stars added. [Data] htmx: +16,800 stars. React: +14,200. That's a meaningful reversal from 2023 where React held the top spot.

What does this tell us? Server-driven, low-JavaScript architectures are not a niche preference. For applications where the server controls state, htmx provides elegance and simplicity that full SPA frameworks simply can't match. [Pause]

React 19 did finally ship in December after three years — with Server Components, Server Functions, and the long-awaited React Compiler. Svelte 5 brought runes for explicit reactive state. Vue 3.5 overhauled its reactivity system. The entire framework layer is in motion.

Key points: (1) htmx overtakes React — HTML-first architectures validated (2) React 19 delivers Server Components and a framework-specification evolution (3) All major frameworks saw meaningful updates in 2024
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 05_react

[Transition] The React ecosystem deserves its own slide because the top projects here tell an interesting story.

shadcn/ui is the #1 React ecosystem project — even though it's not React-exclusive. It works with any framework. That's a signal that the most-loved React tooling is actually heading toward framework agnosticism, mirroring React's own evolution.

Excalidraw at #2 represents a different category entirely — collaborative visual tools. Payload at #3 is a fullstack Next.js CMS framework, reflecting the growing demand for opinionated full-stack solutions.

The meta-point here is Robin Wieruch's observation: React is becoming a specification that frameworks implement differently, not a standalone library you install and use directly. Next.js, Remix, and Gatsby all interpret React's primitives in distinct ways. That's healthy for the ecosystem, but it does mean teams need to choose their React flavor intentionally.

Key points: (1) shadcn/ui leads despite framework-agnostic design (2) React 19 marks a full-stack pivot (3) React-as-specification shift requires intentional framework choice
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 06_vue

[Transition] Vue often gets overlooked in ecosystem trend discussions, but the 2024 data tells a story of quiet maturation.

Nuxt leads with +6,200 stars, followed by PrimeVue, Slidev, the shadcn-vue port, and VitePress. These are quality-first tools: production frameworks, enterprise UI libraries, documentation generators. Not viral toy projects.

Vue 3.5 shipped a full reactivity overhaul, adopting the lighter alien-signals approach — with measurable improvements to memory and performance. Daniel Roe, the Nuxt core team lead, highlighted the active release cadence and consistent performance improvements as key drivers of confidence.

[Data] The absolute star counts are lower than React's ecosystem — roughly one-third the scale — but that's a reflection of Vue's smaller community, not its quality. When your ecosystem starts spawning high-quality UI library alternatives like shadcn-vue, that's a maturity signal.

Key points: (1) Vue ecosystem is quality-driven: production frameworks, enterprise UI, documentation tools (2) Vue 3.5 reactivity overhaul is a technical step change (3) Lower absolute stars vs React reflects community size, not ecosystem health
Duration: 1.5 minutes

---

# 07_themes

[Transition] Stepping back from specific frameworks, three cross-cutting themes defined JavaScript development in 2024.

First, AI is now infrastructure. [Data] n8n at +17k, Flowise at +14.5k, Supabase at +14.5k — these aren't just popular tools, they're the plumbing for AI-native applications. Four of the top 10 overall projects have significant AI capabilities. If your library or platform doesn't have an AI story in 2025, you're already behind.

Second, web technology is going native. Tauri at +15.9k continues its push to let web developers ship desktop and mobile applications with a fraction of Electron's resource overhead. This matters: it expands the addressable surface of every frontend team's skills.

Third, the browser is becoming a platform tier in its own right. PGlite runs full Postgres via WebAssembly in a browser tab. WebVM runs an entire virtual machine. These aren't demos — they're signals of where local-first, offline-first architectures are heading. [Pause]

Key points: (1) AI integration: table stakes for any new tooling in 2025 (2) Tauri makes web tech a native target (3) WASM transforms the browser into a compute platform
Duration: 2 minutes

---

# 08_takeaways

[Transition] So what do all of these trends add up to? Let me give you five takeaways you can bring back to your teams.

One: own your components. The copy-paste model isn't just a UI preference, it's an architectural stance. Teams that adopt it gain maintainability and customization. Watch the registry ecosystem closely.

Two: HTML-first is production-ready. If you're building server-driven apps, evaluate htmx. The ecosystem is real, the philosophy is sound, and the developer experience is excellent.

Three: React is becoming a spec. If your team is on React, you need to pick your framework intentionally. Next.js, Remix, and others differ meaningfully in how they implement React 19's primitives.

Four: every new tool you adopt should have an AI story. AI isn't a feature to add later — it needs to be part of your evaluation criteria today.

Five: don't sleep on Vue. If you're choosing between frameworks for a new project, Vue's ecosystem maturity — combined with the Vue 3.5 performance improvements — makes it a first-class option.

[Pause] The overarching theme? JavaScript continues to expand what's possible: from AI workflows to native apps to in-browser compute. 2025 will be a year of consolidation and deepening in all three of these vectors.

Key points: (1) Five actionable takeaways for 2025 planning (2) Component ownership, HTML-first, React-as-spec, AI-native, Vue maturity (3) JS ecosystem is expanding its surface area — teams need deliberate choices
Duration: 2 minutes
